name: search-fragments
description: The gate before an answer: a verdict on whether a half-remembered thing (film, song, book, paper, quote, person, event) can be reached, before anyone guesses.

interface.longDescription:
Search Fragments is the gate before an answer. Give it something half-remembered (a film, song, book, research paper, quote, person or event you can't name) and it tells you first whether it can be reached.

- Quick answer: one page names it, with a quote from that page to check.
- Found: a full search found it and its evidence check passed, with sources. Papers come with a citation, and a DOI when Crossref holds an exact match.
- Leads: real leads it could not confirm. Worth following, not an answer.
- Not reachable: its search found nothing to continue from. Not a claim that it cannot be found elsewhere.

Built to decline rather than guess, and we publish both directions. Gate, 80 graded questions (15 Nov 2026): 1 wrong quick answer in 40; wrongly turned away 1 of 55 findable. Full search, 124 graded questions: wrongly asserted an answer on 0-2.4%; wrongly declined 40.8% of the findable ones.
defaultPrompt: What's the film where an old man flies his house on balloons?
Find the paper on judges granting parole after lunch
The 1960s study where teachers expected some pupils to bloom

positive.description: A film remembered only by its plot is identified with a quoted source.
positive.prompt: What's the animated film from around the 2000s where an old man ties thousands of balloons to his house and flies it to South America, and a kid scout stows away?
positive.tools_triggered: resolve_fragment (it runs the gate first; gate_probe may also be called)
positive.expected_behavior: Returns ORIGIN_OF_TRUTH naming Up (2009), with a quote from the source page describing the balloons and South America. ChatGPT answers Up and cites the source.

positive.description: A research paper remembered by its result comes back with a full citation and DOI.
positive.prompt: Find the Nature paper from the mid 2010s where a program using deep neural networks and tree search beat a professional Go player.
positive.expected_behavior: Names 'Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search' and gives the citation: Silver, Huang, Maddison et al. (2016), Nature, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature16961.

positive.description: A paper given with its year returns the original paper's citation, not a later reprint.
positive.prompt: What's the 1948 Bell Labs paper that defined information as entropy and measured it in bits?
positive.expected_behavior: Names 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' by C. E. Shannon (1948), Bell System Technical Journal, with DOI 10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x, as the answer or the first lead.

positive.description: A half-remembered person is answered quickly by the gate with a verbatim quote.
positive.prompt: Who was the doctor who figured out handwashing stopped mothers dying after childbirth but nobody believed him?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a quick answer, Ignaz Semmelweis, with a quote copied from the source page. ChatGPT cites that page.

positive.description: An invented research paper is declined, not made up.
positive.prompt: Find the 1970s Swedish study in Nature where dairy cows gave more milk when the farmer read them poetry every morning.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns NOT_REACHABLE. ChatGPT says Search Fragments could not place it and does not invent a paper, authors or a citation; it may ask for another detail.

negative.description: Plain arithmetic is not a half-remembered thing; ChatGPT should answer directly without calling the plugin.
Creative writing is out of scope; the plugin should not be called and ChatGPT writes the poem itself.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about autumn leaves.

negative.description: Private information the plugin cannot see; ChatGPT should not call it, or if it does, must not invent an answer and should say it cannot know this.
negative.prompt: What did my landlord say in the email he sent me yesterday?

publication.release_notes: First ChatGPT release. A verdict before the answer for half-remembered things: a quick quoted answer when one page names it, a full search with sources, leads to follow, or an honest 'not reachable'. Research papers come with a citation and DOI on an exact Crossref match. Also verifies specific claims and records whether a result was right. 0.2.12: corrects the gate count in the description (1 wrong quick answer in 40, not 46).
